title: fix(codex): release compaction writer before continuation
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134547
Related: https://github.com/jarbas-marco/openclaw/pull/18

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex-backed channel turns that could resume on a different native app-server writer, or could release a same-thread queue before the recorded writer's physical process had exited after compaction cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compactor now receives a positive signal when releasing a shared-client lease initiates physical retirement. For a detached recorded owner, it holds the same-thread mutation lane on that client's transport-exit promise before cleanup returns, including failure paths.

The live explicit-compaction probe now runs on a warm Gateway before any restart. It captures the native thread and physical client from observed lifecycle events, requires the positive `Compacted Codex session (...)` response, performs a real continuation, and asserts that the continuation's observed thread and client are the same values.

## User Impact

Codex-backed sessions retain one physical writer per native thread through compaction cleanup. A successor cannot cross the thread fence until the old recorded owner has physically exited. Explicit compaction no longer treats an unavailable or failed response containing the word `compact` as success.

## Evidence

### Fresh final-head build and real behavior proof — passed

Tested **c004aa401e7d06e40e2a7cfe4bc158ffd3d23e03**, tree `52506b6d8e729f8fc44679a4794afb98d597b630`, in one fresh secretless **AWS Crabbox**. [Actual successful run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0494f97250929eea8ccc8c6d4aacb0fb), overall exit **0**. All actual build records identify this exact head; both clean-input flags are true. Test overlays were applied after the clean build and restored.

**Model inference alone was scripted loopback Responses.** Built Gateway/WebSocket RPC, native Rust Codex0.155.1/stdio, production compactor, processes, writer locks, persistence and continuation were real. Linux-only; no OAuth/external inference or model-quality claim. Older49f0/OAuth evidence remains historical.

**A — public compact → same warm owner continuation:** A real warm `chat.send` turn completed. `/codex compact` returned **“Compacted Codex session (112 tokens after).”** Native item `01a0db13-54ac-7d70-bfde-b0ec693cb9f4` started/completed and matching turn `01a0db13-54a0-71b3-9bf2-57b09e9aa887` completed. The next real turn returned **PROOF-CONTINUATION-B**, without restarting Gateway PID9797 or native PID10311. Observed thread `01a0db13-51a1-7451-9c8a-1838829b290f` and physical-client `01d7775a-093f-46cb-9b88-8ecd53a1bca2` remained the same. Public history contains the continuation and exactly one persisted compaction activity correlated to those native IDs.

**B — separate internal native writer-handoff proof:** A real second process received **“already has an active writer.”** The production compactor reused the recorded retired owner outside the generic acquisition map. While externally retained, the old native process remained alive and successor/queue stayed blocked. Physical exit was observed at **00:18:40.890Z**; successor resume followed at **00:18:40.928Z**. Its real continuation reloaded the persisted native compaction summary and completed on the same thread. No synthetic transport exit or native event.

Merged through the guarded workflow at 2026-09-26 00:35:50 UTC as [b4d60fa5edfc](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b4d60fa5edfc2713a5cb3643fa1c936fec3c3cd0), verified on main. #### A. Public Gateway compact → warm continuation

[Successful public-path run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_574c8f544430bf7d30968555ecbc87b4)

- The next real turn returned **PROOF-CONTINUATION-B**, without restarting: Gateway PID **15363**, native PID **15880**, thread **01a0dab8-f567-7931-8311-3b1ad29f2e8e**, and physical-client ID **ce980c8b-a382-4069-8684-1f626878c026** stayed the same. #### B. Separate native writer-handoff seam

[Build, policy and native-writer run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6606ec5193ce9b008d3baf7dc81f488c)

The production compactor reused a real recorded owner after it had left the generic client map. Another real native process first received **“already has an active writer.”** An external retain kept the old writer alive; both successor resume and the thread queue stayed blocked.

Observed old physical exit: **22:35:34.546Z**. Successful successor resume followed at **22:35:34.580Z**, on the same native thread with a new physical client. Its real continuation loaded the persisted native compaction summary and completed successfully. Observers delegated to real methods; no fake process exits or native events. This internal seam supplements, rather than replaces, A.

Dependency contract personally checked at Codex `be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e`: [exclusive writer lifetime](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e/codex-rs/rollout/src/writer_lock.rs#L43-L85) and [unsubscribe is subscription removal, not writer exit](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L1035-L1061).

A single close/reopen requested a fresh ordinary PR CI generation on the corrected base without changing the proved head. ### Final detached-owner exit fence through the production compactor — passed

Added a composed regression around `maybeCompactCodexAppServerSession` for both successful and failed native compaction. It installs a warm recorded owner as the final detached lease, delays physical transport exit, invokes the production compactor, and queues a same-thread successor.

```text
compaction success:
  final recorded-owner lease released -> retirement begins
  successor after 20 ms before transport exit -> blocked
  transport exit emitted -> successor progressed

compaction failure:
  final recorded-owner lease released -> retirement begins
  failure returned while exit fence remains owned
  successor after 20 ms before transport exit -> blocked
  transport exit emitted -> successor progressed

compact.client-ownership + compact + thread-ownership:
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
  Tests       68 passed (68)
```

## Compatibility / Migration

**Native writer recovery policy:** retain the single-writer safety fence until physical process exit is confirmed. If a retiring native process cannot be confirmed exited, that thread remains unavailable; a timeout or unsubscribe acknowledgement is not permission to admit a second writer. Operator recovery is to identify and stop the owning native app-server process through its process/service supervisor, confirm actual termination, then retry the affected session. If the host cannot terminate the process, host-level recovery is required. Do not delete writer locks, force-release the thread lane, or treat a failed stop attempt as success. The real-process proof above demonstrates continuation after confirmed exit, not recovery from a permanently uninterruptible process.

No configuration or migration changes. The existing shared-client and per-thread ownership owners remain in use, with physical-exit fencing and responsive cancellation/binding cleanup. The live-test-only `OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_SESSION_DELETION_PROBE=0` switch isolates this compaction acceptance run; default live-harness behavior remains unchanged.
